stem: One carpenter can build a cabinet in 12 days. How many days will 3 carpenters take to build it if they all work at the same rate?
hints: More workers means fewer days. Should the answer be bigger or smaller than 12?
One carpenter builds 1/12 of the cabinet per day. Three carpenters build 3 times as much per day.
Find what 3 carpenters build per day (3 × 1/12), simplify, then flip the fraction to get the days.

solution.methodName: Work rates: rate = 1 ÷ time, then add the rates

steps.action: Let x = the number of days 3 carpenters need.
One carpenter's rate: 1/12 of the cabinet per day.
steps.why: A whole job done in 12 days means 1/12 of it each day.

steps.action: Three carpenters: 3 × 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the cabinet per day.

steps.why: If they build 1/4 of the cabinet each day, they need 4 days for the whole cabinet.

steps.action: Check: 3 carpenters × 4 days = 12 days of work, the same as 1 carpenter × 12 days. They need 4 days.

trapNotes.9: This is 12 − 3. Three workers do 3 times as much each day, so divide by 3.
trapNotes.15: This is 12 + 3. More workers means fewer days, not more.
trapNotes.36: This multiplies 12 × 3. More workers finish faster, so the number of days must go down.
